In fact, he was planning to have General Wiley and his people fight on the frontlines, then promote Khaslana, who was mixed in, so he wouldn't draw the Kremnoan family's attention.

Of course, in the emperor's expectations, other people would be in charge of fighting; Khaslana only needed to stay safe under others' protection.

But things weren't so smooth. Although General Wiley was said to be strong, the biggest reason he had fought the Zerg back in the past was because of the other side's scheming.

Besides, someone the Kremnoan family placed at the emperor's side had already discovered Khaslana's true identity.

Even if Nanook didn't act, the people behind him in the Kremnoan family wouldn't let things go. They would set up all kinds of obstacles for Khaslana, trying to make it difficult for Khaslana to survive. After all, it was incredibly easy to off someone in somewhere as chaotic as the frontiers of the empire.

Phainon wasn't worried for Khaslana at all. This was the plot from the original novel anyways. Next, as all kinds of people chased after him with the intent to kill, Khaslana would grow stronger and stronger, then at the frontier he would gather several teammates who were strong but had no status. Not long after coming back, he would approach the finale.

Phainon felt emotional when he thought about how he was finally going to be able to leave the world. He had only stayed a few months in this world, but so many things had happened. It made him feel like he had been here for ages. But a strange part of him also felt melancholic about those moments but he pushed that thought to the back of his brain.

Ever since the engagement banquet, Phainon was forced to live with Nanook. He even had to learn palace etiquette and such during the day.

He was just about to leave, but he still couldn't scrape by... Because every night, Nanook insisted on inspecting what Phainon studied. If Phainon couldn't answer, he would ‘punish’ Phainon.

Phainon seriously suspected that Nanook was just finding an excuse, but he couldn't do anything about it. He could only use the passion he had for learning about mechas to learn palace etiquette.

Phainon ate listlessly after tiring himself out with his studies. Maybe Nanook was insisting on competing with Mydei, because he was always cooking personally. It made Phainon, who had thought he would be able to eat palace delicacies, extremely disappointed.

"Did you know? The child that Father truly loves is that Khaslana guy." Nanook looked at Phainon, propping up his head with hand. He said slowly, "He must be happy."

Under the candlelight, his face was stunningly beautiful. Phainon still felt that getting engaged with Nanook was too much of a fantasy. It took him a long moment to react to what was being said.

"Of course I didn't know," Phainon said quickly. "Still, Khaslana really is pretty awesome."

Was it possible for fate's favorite in a novel not to be awesome? Though Khaslana tragically lost to Phainon several times and even got stabbed by Phainon several times.

Nanook continued, "Also, Mydeimos went to the frontier with those people as well."

"Huh?" Phainon was a bit shocked. He suddenly remembered what Mydei said to him the day of the engagement banquet.

In the original novel, Mydei worshipped Khaslana, so he couldn't feel at ease letting him go alone, and followed along... This time, he had probably decided to leave and go out to improve himself after being provoked by Nanook.

This world's consciousness was amazing... It could even make the plot develop the same way as the original novel_(:3」∠)_ "As the heir of the Kremnoan family's next generation, he clearly doesn't have to worry about his future. Why would he take a risk and go to the frontier?" Nanook asked. "Is it to train himself, or is it for something else?"

Phainon hurriedly said, "Of course it's to train himself. After all, Mydei is someone who seeks strength."

"You're right, but... Don't you think you understand things related to him too well?" Nanook smiled slightly. "Didn't I tell you before? You need to forget everything about him."

This kind of thing isn't something you can forget just by saying you'd forget!

Phainon quickly changed the topic. He asked, "But, Your Highness, what exactly is your goal in having those low-level Zerg do these kinds of things..."

"Of course it's for my amusement," Nanook said. "Isn't it fun? You can see what the lofty nobles would look like when they're afraid. It's enjoyable just thinking about it."

Phainon: "..." Was there really nothing wrong with people like Nanook who thought like this!!

---

As expected, things progressed pretty much as they did in the original novel. In just a few months, the Zerg looked like they were going to retreat.

Though the generals fighting at the frontiers didn't get lavish praise for being heroes who saved the empire like last time, they received plenty of flattery, especially Khaslana. He was young and handsome, and he had made plenty of contributions. For a moment, he was the most dazzling person in the empire. Several people suddenly realized that Khaslana was someone who had fought his way into the finals of the mecha competition when they found the videos of him online.

After all, only the first place winner would be remembered by the people, and the first place winner Prince Latiao was so flashy that it made Khaslana's brilliance significantly dimmer.

But now there had been no news of Prince Latiao for a long time. In contrast, Khaslana was on the way to taking his place.

Many people wondered why someone as strong as Prince Latiao wouldn't publicize his identity... And General Wiley, who had kept his grudges the entire time, took the chance to get a group of people to guide public opinion online.

For a moment, several people began to say that although Prince Latiao was strong, he had no courage. At such a critical moment, he didn't have the guts to come out. He couldn't hold a candle to Khaslana.

Mydei had achieved plenty himself, and because he went personally to the frontlines to kill the Zerg despite being the heir of the Kremnoan family, he won a good amount of the common populace's heart.

But this was all to pave the way for Khaslana, and similarly all the propaganda focused on him. Most of the time, Mydei was overlooked.

The emperor was put at ease. He moved directly to confer a title on Khaslana, giving him a position with real power and promoting him rapidly. The others were also awarded generously, but they didn't get anything close to Khaslana. Many people immediately thought about how to get close to Khaslana.

General Wiley suffered serious injuries in the expedition. When he recovered, he was still far from his past strength. He immediately thought of resting, and he passed on all of his influence and subordinates to Khaslana.

In that span of time, Khaslana's power and influence faintly became greater than what General Wiley's had been. Although he couldn't compare to the Kremnoan family, he was already enough to give them a sense of danger.

There had also been several scandals from the Kremnoan family recently. After all, there was no way that they had reached such greatness cleanly. It was obvious just by looking at how Herklas had tried to use the Kremnoan family's name the other time. It was just that nobody had ever dared to oppose them or speak up in the past.

But this time, the person behind the people spreading the news was the emperor. Of course, they were assured with him as their support. At the same time, the Kremnoan family had never expected that the trick they used against General Wiley could be used against them. Soon, they were in a bad spot.

---

Nobody would expect Khaslana and his subordinates that the place normally met to discuss was an extremely ordinary residence on a remote outer planet.

Wearing a disguise, Mydei walked in after getting off the aircar. "What did you call me here for?"

"I want to show you something very interesting." Khaslana pushed open an interior door, smiling slightly, and a Zerg corpse appeared in front of them. Although it looked slightly different from an ordinary Zerg, there wasn't anything special about it.

Mydei had seen plenty of them on the frontier. He said coolly, "It's just a Zerg corpse. What am I supposed to be looking at?"

"It's different from other Zergs," Khaslana said. "When it was alive, it looked like a human."

"What?" Mydei felt a sense of alarm. He looked carefully at the Zerg's corpse, but no matter how he studied it, he couldn't see anything unusual.

"It happened a few days ago. I caught someone who wanted to assassinate me and brought him here to interrogate," Khaslana said. "I didn't expect that after he died, this fellow would turn into a Zerg... It really is interesting."

Mydei knew perfectly well that most of the people who came to assassinate Khaslana were sent by the Kremnoan family, and his expression turned grave.

After what happened in the past, he understood that, although he was the heir of the most powerful Kremnoan family, in reality the power was out of his hands. The family had never even taken him seriously.

He wanted to make his way up and get revenge on Nanook, who had snatched away his everything, so he had come to the frontier, making peace with the person who had the same goal as him, Khaslana. Of course, they each had their own plans.

But on the road, all kinds of things kept happening. All kinds of people came on assassination missions. There was someone who wanted to kill Khaslana in every situation. But Khaslana was truly lucky; he was able to push through each and every assassination. Mydei had the feeling that he was someone favored by the heavens.

"What is going on here..." Mydei frowned slightly. "How could there be a Zerg who took the shape of a human?"

"I thought it was strange before. These Zerg were just like ordinary beasts... But suddenly, they could show high intelligence. Thus, it made people suspect that they were separated into different categories," Khaslana said. "I had people study this corpse. Although it looks no different from a normal Zerg on the outside, it's actually several times stronger than a normal Zerg... If it wasn't for the fact that it died when it was returning to its normal form, even I would have trouble dealing with it.

"I looked into it more after that, and I discovered some very interesting things."

Khaslana pulled out a sheaf of papers. They were filled with information about people who had been awarded recognition of their service in the war years ago. Today, they had all climbed to lofty positions in the empire. The one thing that matched between all of them was that they were on the crown prince's side.

"These people," Mydei said, "are all childless?"

"Exactly. All of these people have been married for several years, but they don't have any children. Why is that?" Khaslana said. "I think we'll certainly make a big discovery if we investigate them."

Mydei said, "What you're saying is that they're all Zerg?"

"I didn't say that," Khaslana said. "But if that's true... then our plans aren't far from success. His Highness the Crown Prince, that high and lofty fellow, has finally given the game away."

"I truly never expected it," Mydei said quietly. "His Highness has actually been colluding with the Zerg."

This was something that could deal a serious blow to the Kremnoan family, but Mydei didn't feel sorrowful at all. Instead, he had a faint sense of excitement.

The Kremnoan family was too strong. They should have stopped existing a long time ago. As long as the family existed, he would be unable to do the things he wanted to do.

And if Nanook fell from power, then wouldn't Phainon also come to his side?

Mydei suddenly found his own thoughts terrifying, but he couldn't completely stop himself.

As long as he could have Phainon return to his side, he didn't care about anything. Nothing could make him hesitate for even a split second.

---

It wasn't just Khaslana and his side who discovered some clues. Problems were also beginning to rise within the empire.

At some point, several people announced with terror that they had seen people turn into Zerg with their own eyes.

At first, everyone thought of those words as utter nonsense. Even the people who said it themselves suspected that they might have gone crazy. Zerg were Zerg and humans were humans. How could a human suddenly turn into a Zerg?

But soon after, pictures unexpectedly surfaced time and time again. In the pictures, the Zerg were very real. Even an expert couldn't tell where the pictures were edited when they examined them.

The major planets began to impose a curfew, and they required several rounds of questioning to leave. Many people who just arrived on the planet were isolated and examined.

General Wiley, who had already retired, took a stand, saying that he had indeed seen some high-level Zerg turning into humans when he went out to war this time, and they were extremely intelligent. He told everyone not to hold everything back and to speak up about anyone who they felt was suspicious.

In moments, everyone was alarmed. Many people stayed home, afraid to go out. They would feel suspicious even when they saw their long-time friends.

But in that moment, Khaslana took a stand. He said that his subordinates had discovered a way to find out if someone was a Zerg pretending to be a human.

As someone who discovered how to deal with the situation, Khaslana was just like how General Wiley had been in the past. He was quickly put up on a pedestal and hailed by everyone as a hero.

And Khaslana worked swiftly and fiercely. As long as someone was suspicious, he would take them in for an examination. He arrested several of the higher-ups in the Kremnoan family, and finally discovered that they really were Zerg.

In moments, the Kremnoan family became public enemy number one. In contrast, the heir of the Kremnoan family Mydei unhesitatingly announced that he was on Khaslana's side.

It was only then that everyone remembered that those people in the Kremnoan family were only replaced because the Zerg killed them. They quickly felt a wave of sympathy for Mydei.

Things happened in rapid succession. Many of the higher-ups in the Kremnoan family died, but it was obvious that they didn't have the same strength they used to have. Naturally, they couldn't compare with Khaslana, who was at the peak of his power.

Soon afterwards, the emperor took the chance to send out an announcement: Khaslana was actually the beloved son he had been separated from for many years.

In the midst of the chaos, Nanook said nothing. He didn't even take a side. Several of his subordinates had been exposed as Zerg, and their strength had been pretty much destroyed. His greatest support, the Kremnoan family, no longer had their old glory.

Soon, many bystanders who valued strength sought refuge with Khaslana. There were people who spoke out to say His Highness the Crown Prince's personality was unsuited to being the heir of the throne, and Khaslana's personality was the most suitable. They demanded that Khaslana was made the crown prince.

Things progressed smoothly. It was going so smoothly that even if Khaslana was fate's favorite it seemed too convenient.

While the outer world was in a hubbub, Nanook was calm. He even had the spare time to help Phainon wash his hair.

"Aren't you worried?" Phainon couldn't help but ask.

Although nobody was saying that Nanook was a Zerg, there were many people that guessed Nanook had some connection to the Zerg... It looked like Nanook's identity would be found out sooner or later.

"Why do I need to worry?" Nanook said, smiling slightly. "Right now, everything is going just as I want it to..."

Phainon: "!?"

Wait! Actually, based on what happened in the original novel, Nanook would be able to achieve his goal of controlling the whole empire if he inherited the throne. Why would he still do so much? Could it be that he really just thought it was fun?

"You must be wondering why I did so many unnecessary things." Nanook could tell what Phainon was thinking at a glance. "To be honest, my goal isn't to rule the empire."

Phainon often felt that Nanook might have the power to read minds. His guesses were simply too accurate.

"In fact, I want to destroy the empire," Nanook said. "Don't you think these people are boring? No matter if they're people or Zerg, it's most interesting when they're facing destruction."

Phainon: "!" Hey, Nanook was totally a chaotic evil villain!

"Actually, the fact that all those people are Zerg... I revealed it to the public. What fun is a chess board where you always have the upper hand?" Nanook said slowly. "Being backed into a corner all by yourself is the only way to have the most fun."

Phainon: "...!" I already stopped understanding what exactly you're having fun with!

But it looked like now... the finale should be coming soon.

No matter what Nanook wanted to do, he just had to endure until the finale and everything would be fine! He could do everything again in the next world.

--- In the next few days, Khaslana's influence grew more and more. In contrast, Nanook declined all visitors, seeming as though he had lost all hope. His subordinates also did nothing.

Just as though it seemed like everything had already been decided, an unforeseen event occurred. On a perfectly normal morning, countless people discovered that their friends or family members had become Zerg.

The entire country flew into a panic.

Everyone had thought that the Zerg had already been captured. But all of the Zerg who had been caught were people that purposely revealed their identities under Nanook's suggestion.

The imperial palace was also in chaos. In the grand hall, the emperor looked at Nanook, his face filled with terror. "What are you trying to do?"

After being on the throne for so many years, the emperor had enjoyed all kinds of pleasures. He said that he missed his true love, but in fact he doted on a number of new lovers. He had never trained; his strength didn't even match up to a twelve-year-old alpha.

"Father, I just want you to pass on with Mother." Nanook smiled slightly. "You don't need to be scared. It will all end quickly."

"I know I can't make it up to your mother..." the emperor said. "But you don't need to go so far either. How have I ever treated you unfairly in these years?"

The emperor took a step back in his terror, but he bumped into Khaslana who was just coming into the door. He immediately stood at Khaslana's side, feeling much more at ease.

"Father, you don't need to worry anymore. Nothing will happen now that I'm here." As Khaslana spoke, he smiled slightly. He skewered a sharp knife through the emperor's chest.

He gazed at the emperor's astounded expression, and he let out the laugh he had been holding back.

"My deepest apologies. I've always hated you."

Even if the emperor was biased towards him, Khaslana's hostility had never changed. Although the Kremnoan family had pushed him towards the slums, it had a lot to do with the emperor... If it wasn't for the fact that he couldn't even protect the woman he loved, how would things go so far?

Khaslana looked at Nanook. "Your Highness the Crown Prince, I didn't expect that you would collude with the Zerg. For the sake of the empire's future, it looks like I have no choice but to make a move against you."

"Oh? If you have the strength, then don't hesitate to come at me." Nanook laughed.

Dozens of Zerg rushed in from outside, gathering up by Nanook.

The Zerg were hideous. Their carapace was as hard as an alloy, and their blood could corrode a mecha. Coupled with their speed, it was difficult for an ordinary person to face them without a mecha.

"It looks like I've underestimated." Khaslana's gaze turned cold. He had no choice but to temporarily withdraw.

---

Phainon didn't realize that the world had turned on its head until he woke up.

Fuck, he just got up a little late! Why did it seem like he missed a lot? Nanook didn't even wake him up at such a critical moment.

Phainon was given a shock. He shot to his feet, making to exit.

But there was a bodyguard that Nanook left at the door. Although he treated Phainon with great respect, he had absolutely no intention to give way.

Phainon knew that all of these bodyguards were originally Zerg. It would be impossible for him to break through by himself, so he had no choice but to return to his room.

He had to find a way to get out, then he would probably be able to leave the world after he found Khaslana. Otherwise, if he stayed here... After the finale, the new emperor Khaslana would probably find someone to kill him off.

Phainon could still remember how he stabbed Khaslana a few times back then. The person that Khaslana hated the most was, without a doubt, him.

Unexpectedly, Phainon heard the sound of fighting from outside. He hid in a place with cover, shocked. He was afraid it was someone Khaslana sent. If he was caught, he would be done for.

The fight ended quickly. The sound of footsteps came over, and at the same time, Mydei's voice sounded.

"I'm here to pick you up."

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 22: The Winner Takes It All
chapters.html:
Phainon immediately let out a breath of relief. He came out. "Why are you here?"

Mydei felt emotional seeing Phainon again. "You're in danger. Of course I must come."

When Phainon thought about how Mydei was working with Khaslana, he knew the time had almost come. He asked, "How are things outside right now?"

Mydei said, "Right now, it's a mess outside. The common people are all staying in shelters. Many Zerg are out on the streets. I feared something would happen to you, so I rushed over.... How about I take you to the shelter now."

Phainon followed Mydei down the stairs. He spotted a Zerg corpse lying on the ground and a mecha before him; his heart suddenly skipped a beat.

"Let me borrow your mecha for a moment."

Mydei was stunned. "What did you say?"

Phainon just placed a kiss on Mydei’s cheek, steeling his heart and whispering “I’m sorry Mydeimos.”

Everything happened too quickly. Before Mydei could react, Phainon leaped into the cockpit of the mecha, whisking it away so quickly it was as though the mecha hadn't even touched the ground.

Although a normal mecha had authentication systems that made it so others couldn't use them at random, Phainon's strong spiritual energy was enough to obliterate the mecha's security and allow him to immediately pilot the mecha.

Phainon rushed towards the main hall. The road was left extremely open. There were barely even any Zerg.

It was a good thing that Nanook lived in the imperial palace, or it might have been a hassle.

While he was on the road, Phainon's personal terminal suddenly lit up. Unexpectedly, a holographic screen appeared without his prompting and began to transmit the scene by the imperial palace.

Phainon immediately froze. The rest of the empire was probably watching the same broadcast. He didn't expect that Nanook would get someone to control the mainframe. On the screen, Nanook sat up straight on the throne. He was wearing a crown on his head, and he looked over with a slight smile. He said, "I think everyone must be very confused, hmm? Don't worry, and don't be scared.... There's already no hope for you."

Phainon: "!" Hey, these lines were exactly like a villain's! It was easy for him to imagine how shocked the public would be at His Highness the Crown Prince's words. Still, this was the effect Nanook wanted....

"I truly apologize for hiding this from you in the past." Nanook sighed. "In truth, I'm a Zerg and human hybrid. And the beautiful empress you remember was actually the transformed Zerg Queen."

Everyone in the shelters was stunned silly when they saw the broadcast. They couldn't believe what they were hearing at all.

"It's really such a pity that Father died too soon; otherwise, if he learnt about this, he would probably be pleasantly surprised," Nanook said. "After all, he lived with the Zerg Queen for such a long time. How difficult for an ordinary human."

Phainon: "..." There was obviously nobody who would be excited about something like this!

Phainon finally hurried his way to the imperial palace. He quickly spotted ten Zerg fighting against Khaslana.

Phainon couldn't actually recognize Khaslana's mecha, but as soon as he spotted it, Phainon heard the system's voice.

[Beep beep beep... Detected an even more powerful character.... Beginning to select capture targets in accordance with the system's regulations.... Selection complete. The current capture target is Khaslana.]

That was so hard! He finally succeeded in binding to the original male lead now!

It was Phainon's first time feeling emotional over binding to someone.

"Then I can leave now, right?" Phainon said. "After all, it's pretty much the finale now."

[The villain boss is not dead yet and the original protagonist has not reached his peak, so the host can't leave yet.]

"Huh?!" But in the original novel Nanook didn't get his lunchbox either!

[Currently, due to his exposed identity, he turned from a villain who could be saved into a villain who must be killed.]

"..." Even this was okay?

Because he thought he'd be able to leave immediately, Phainon had relaxed. He didn't bother paying attention to how long he had been maneuvering the mecha at all. After the shock, Phainon suddenly felt his body go stiff. Blood began to flow out of his mouth.

"Fuck!" It had already been more than five minutes! Hey, his body was about to collapse!

On the other side, Khaslana made a mistake and was accidentally splashed with the Zerg's corrosive body fluids. Instantly, his movements slowed. It was obvious that for the time being there was no way he would be able to charge over to Nanook and begin a life-or-death battle.

Phainon: "!?" Fuck, something would actually happen at such a critical moment? He wasn't going to get his lunchbox at such a critical moment, right?

No, he still had hope.

Phainon gritted his teeth. There was still one person who could kill Nanook, and that person was him.

Phainon maneuvered the mecha with gritted teeth, passing Khaslana and charging at Nanook.

He had never wanted to be a hero. He had never wanted any of this—not the system, not the endless transmigration, not the cruel joke of falling for people he could never keep.

Especially not him.

The thought of Mydei flashed through his mind unbidden: those sunset eyes, the way he would kneel with such fierce devotion, the gentle hands that had learned to cook just to make Phainon happy. The way he had looked when Phainon kissed him goodbye just moments ago.

"I'm sorry, Mydeimos."

The words felt like glass in his throat.

His silhouette of course appeared on the screen. Everyone could recognize Mydeimos's mecha, and they immediately roused themselves with excitement, telling themselves that the empire still had hope.

"Oh?" Nanook looked at the mecha in front of him. "It's someone familiar. Still, even if it's someone familiar, I won't show any mercy."

Immediately, numerous Zerg swarmed in from the sidelines, blitzing at the mecha.

Phainon used his spiritual energy to feel all around him, as though he had temporarily forgotten how his body was about to collapse. With natural, easy movements, he cut down the Zerg who flung themselves at him. Every attack was precisely on his enemy's weak points, cutting the Zerg right in two.

But he wouldn't be able to stand up against the increasingly serious condition of his body even if he was more skilled, and it was like he would never kill enough of the surrounding Zerg.

Moreover, when the Zerg died, the corrosive fluids from their bodies would splash onto the mecha. At first, it wasn't a problem, but with the buildup of more fluids, significant amounts of the mecha eroded.

Phainon coughed up another mouthful of blood. The scene in front of him turned blurry.

"!" Fuck! Even if Khaslana came personally to flaunt his protagonist halo he might not be able to kill Nanook!

This same scene was broadcasted to the entire empire. Everyone saw it as clear as day.

"Amazing..."

"But is Lord Mydeimos so strong?"

Anyone who was more in the know about mechas could tell that though the mecha before their eyes belonged to Mydei, its movements were completely different from Mydei's. Even if Mydei had purposely concealed his strength in the past, it was impossible that it could be to this extent.

"Maybe it's some expert in his mecha. These movements look so familiar!"

"I remember now! Didn't Prince Latiao use these kinds of moves before?!"

"Yes, exactly! They really are the same... Could it be that the person inside is Prince Latiao?"

Everyone began to feel excited. After all, Prince Latiao was someone so powerful that he could even overthrow General Wiley with ease, so the people in front of him would be a piece of cake.

Phainon gritted his teeth, pulling his spiritual energy back in.

Immediately, the mecha stopped. Just as everyone began to grow doubtful, the door of the cockpit opened. Phainon, his brow dripping in cold sweat and his mouth still gushing with blood, poked out his head.

At that moment, everyone was stupefied.

They all knew this person.... Wasn't this Phainon who everyone had cursed out? How did he get in the mecha?!

Could it be that he was the legendary Prince Latiao? Prince Latiao was a freaking beta?

Nanook immediately stood from his throne.

The Zerg below made to attack, but they felt something, and one by one they stepped back.

Phainon crawled out of the cockpit with difficulty, falling weakly to the ground, but Nanook propped him up.

Nanook looked at Phainon and could immediately see that there was something off. "Your body can't stand it anymore. Why?"

"I...." Phainon didn't finish his sentence even after a long time. He coughed up a mouthful of blood.

He gritted his teeth. He knew that he was about to die. He threw himself into Nanook's chest, pulling out a knife he had hidden on his body for self-defense, and stabbed forward.

Even if Nanook was a Zerg-human hybrid, when he was in his human form, his weakness was his heart.

Before the knife could touch his skin, Nanook caught Phainon by the wrist.

"You want to kill me?" Nanook asked.

Phainon bit his lip. He felt like he was about to be done for. His voice was low. "Exactly...."

Shockingly, Nanook revealed a slight smile. "Of course you can." It was as though he had heard Phainon bring up an ordinary wish. He reached out to grasp Phainon's wrist, thrusting down towards his own chest.

Phainon looked up in astonishment. "Why?"

"Because I like you. I would agree to any of your requests...." Nanook pulled Phainon into his arms. "And... I'm feeling a little tired too. Wouldn't it be the most joyful thing to die with you?"

Although Nanook thought a bit differently from an ordinary person, Phainon had a strange feeling. In the next moment, he completely lost consciousness in Nanook's arms.

[Beep beep beep…. Mission Complete…. Initiating Transfer….]

Phainon’s spirit which was slowly fading away, looked at the corpse of the body he occupied below and felt a strange sensation in his chest. It was good that he was finally able to leave this crazy world but just then a certain blonde haired male came into his mind but he pushed that thought down. He always knew he was going to leave; it was better not to get attached. Mydeimos would be better off without him….. Just as he was thinking this he caught a glimpse of that very person.

When Khaslana came in and saw what happened, he was stunned.

And Mydei, who hurried over, charged over furiously and embraced Phainon's corpse.

He didn't remember crossing the threshold. He didn't remember pushing past the Zerg that had gone suddenly still, their connection to their queen severed. He didn't remember Khaslana shouting something behind him.

All he remembered was the body.

Phainon lay crumpled against Nanook's chest, the crown prince's blood pooling around them both. His eyes were closed, lashes dark against too-pale cheeks.

"Phainon?"

Mydei's voice didn't sound like his own. It was too small, too broken, too human.

He fell to his knees beside the body, hands reaching out to touch—to hold —to somehow undo what had been done.

"Wake up."

His fingers brushed Phainon's cheek. It was still warm.

"Please."

Nothing. No flutter of eyelids, no teasing smile, no exasperated sigh.

"You can't leave me here all alone."

The words tore from his throat, raw and desperate. Mydei gathered Phainon into his arms, pressing him against his chest as if he could force life back into that broken body through sheer will alone.

"I love you."

He had never said it before. He had been too afraid, too reverent, too certain that Phainon would disappear if he spoke the words aloud.

"I love you, I love you, I love you—"

The mantra became a sob. Mydei buried his face in Phainon's hair, breathing in the fading scent of him—that impossible mix of omega sweetness and something uniquely Phainon.

"You idiot." Mydei's tears fell onto Phainon's face, tracing paths through the blood and dirt. "You absolute idiot. Did you think I would want to live in a world without you?"

Mydei pressed his head against Phainon’s chest as if willing his heart to beat once more through sheer force of will. He felt his heart growing colder and colder by the second as he clutched Phainon’s body to his chest.

Just then, his gaze landed on the knife still clutched in Phainon's hand.

Phainon saw this scene and his eyes widened as his heart pounded in his ear drums.

“Mydeimos! Wait- System, what is he doing!? Why isn’t somebody stopping him!”

Phainon had wanted to bury his feelings and leave this world behind but he didn’t want Mydei to be hurt, he wanted him to be healthy and well, to maybe even fall in love with someone else and be happy. But Mydei couldn’t hear him and he was fading fast.

Mydei stared at the knife and then at his dear Deliverer and his heart had made its decision. He grabbed the knife and thrust it towards his own chest.

“Mydei-!” Phainon called out, his hand reaching out.

[Beep beep beep…. Transfer Complete]

That was the last sound Phainon heard as his world went dark and his outstretched hand faded into particles.

Khaslana quickly had his subordinates stop Mydei, knocking him out, then had some people tidy up the main hall. Phainon's corpse was left in the inner hall.

When everyone finally left, Khaslana walked slowly over to the corpse.

Even now he couldn't believe that Phainon, the person who had always opposed him, the person who had won several times against him, had actually died.

His chest felt empty. He couldn't say a single word.

---

After Nanook died, the strength of all the Zerg decreased significantly to the point that even an ordinary human could stand up to them. As such, the crisis that the original novel thought would send the empire into destruction was resolved.

Naturally, Khaslana became the emperor, and he promoted the people who had followed him from the beginning. Only Mydei left without saying goodbye; nobody knew where he went.

Unlike Mydei, Caelus spent several days at Phainon's tombstone, then invested all of his energy into mecha training.

Nobody had expected that in the end, the person who would rescue the empire would be the person that everyone hated, Phainon.

And the truth that Phainon was actually an omega hiding his identity only came out after his death.

It was only then that everyone understood why Prince Latiao only appeared online while staying so lowkey in the real world. After all, he was just an omega.

But though he was just an omega, he stepped out bravely at such a time. He didn't hesitate to sacrifice himself to save the empire. He was completely worthy of being called a hero.

When Phainon's initial engagement with Mydei was brought out, everyone's imaginations ran wild. They even thought that Phainon had known Nanook's identity ages ago, so he laid down his life to hide at Nanook's side.

It was also after this that the empire developed a new medication to remove a mark on an omega, as well as other relatively harmless suppressants.

Their status also rose significantly. They could even attend the same schools as alphas and betas. Soon, there were many more omegas who came to participate in the virtual mecha competitions.

And several hundred years later, the story of Phainon was recorded in the empire's textbooks, and what he did had been shot as several movies.

---

Epilogue:

The apartment was too quiet.

Phainon sat down near his front door, tying his shoes and tried to remember what normal felt like. The morning light slanted through half-open blinds, catching dust motes that drifted lazily through the air. Somewhere outside, a car honked. A bird sang. The world went on, utterly indifferent to the fact that he had lived—and died—in places this world would never know.

He ran a hand through his hair and sighed.

Multiple worlds. Multiple lifetimes of memories. And for what?

The System had been silent since he woke up in his original body three weeks ago. No daily tasks. No electric shocks. No cheerful announcements about capture targets or powerful characters. Just... nothing. Like it had never existed at all.

Good riddance.

But it had still been hard to assimilate back into his modern life when he to the people here he had only been gone a day while he had lived hundreds of years with the system.

Stop it, he told himself. It's over. You're home. Move on.

He'd been telling himself that for three weeks.

It wasn't working.

---

The coffee shop was two blocks away, a small corner place he'd walked past a hundred times before the System snatched him away. It was familiar in the way old shoes were familiar—nothing special, but comfortable. The kind of place where the barista knew your order and the same old man sat in the same corner booth every morning, reading the same newspaper.

Phainon pushed open the door, bell jingling overhead, and stepped inside.

The warmth hit him first—the smell of roasted beans, the hiss of the espresso machine, the low murmur of conversation. It was aggressively, mundanely normal. Exactly what he needed.

He was halfway to the counter when the door swung open behind him.

He didn't think anything of it. Just another customer, here for their morning caffeine fix. He took another step—

And someone crashed into him from the side.

Coffee spilled. The world tilted. Phainon's feet tangled with someone else's, and suddenly he was falling, his shoulder hitting the floor hard, a curse already forming on his lips.

"I'm so sorry—"

The voice stopped him cold.

He knew that voice. He had heard it whisper his name in the dark, had heard it praise him without any scruples, had heard it beg him to wake up when everything was already over.

Phainon looked up.

Blonde hair, a shade lighter than he remembered. Amber eyes, warm as sunset, wide with genuine embarrassment. A face that was all sharp angles and quiet strength, softened now by faint concern spreading across his features.

Mydeimos.

But not his Mydei.

This Mydei wore a simple grey sweater, sleeves pushed up to his elbows. A messenger bag hung across his chest. His hair was shorter, neater, without the warrior's wildness. And his eyes—those eyes that had once blazed with fanatical devotion—were looking at Phainon with nothing but stranger's concern.

"I didn't see you—are you alright?" He crouched down, extending a hand. "Here, let me help you up."

Phainon stared at that hand.

He had watched this man kneel before him in a dozen different ways. Had felt those fingers trace his skin, had held that hand in the dark, had memorized every line and callus. He had watched him fall apart over a body that wasn't even really his.

And now—

Now Mydei was just a stranger in a coffee shop, offering a hand because it was the polite thing to do.

Phainon didn't move.

"Hey?" Mydei's brow furrowed. His hand stayed outstretched, patient but starting to look uncertain. "You okay? Did you hit your head?"

Say something, Phainon screamed at himself. Move. Breathe. Do something normal. This is not him.

Instead, he just kept staring.

Phainon, immersed in his own thought didn’t notice that behind Mydei's polite concern, beneath the unfamiliar sweater and the stranger's confusion, there was something else. A flicker. A pull. A tension in his shoulders that said he felt something, even if he didn't understand it.

Slowly—almost trembling—he reached up and took Mydei's hand.

The grip was warm. Solid. Real.

Mydei pulled him to his feet with easy strength, and for a moment they stood face to face, closer than strangers should stand. Phainon could smell him—coffee and something clean, like soap or rain. Nothing like the battlefield. Nothing like the crown prince's palace.

But the hand holding his didn't let go.

Their eyes met.

And Mydei hesitated.

His lips parted, then closed. His head tilted, just a fraction, as if he was trying to solve a puzzle he didn't have the pieces for.

"Sorry," he said again, but this time his voice was quieter. "Do I... know you?"

"You seem..." Mydei trailed off, searching for a word that didn't seem to exist. "Familiar."
